function: Radar-assisted uplink channel estimation for mmWave massive MIMO in V2X: Radar-CEnet deep unfolding recovers the sparse angle-domain channel using radar DOA prior from MAML-CNN (p. 1, p. 7).
system: V2X road-side unit with 64-antenna ULA and 4 RF chains, 3 single-antenna vehicles, 64 subcarriers, 28 GHz; separate 16-element monostatic radar array; no RIS (pp. 3, 10).
method: Radar-CEnet: LISTA-GS-based deep unfolding, 15 layers, new prior-support soft-threshold, supervised MSE training; MAML-CNN meta-learning with fine-tuning for DOA under imperfect arrays (pp. 5-8, 11).
data_channel: Custom geometric mmWave channel with Gaussian path gains (p. 4); also 3GPP TR 38.901 CDL-E data from Sionna: 50,000 train, 3,000 validation, 3,000 test samples (p. 13).
test_conditions: MAML-CNN: meta-trained on 100 imperfect-array tasks, then fine-tuned on new arrays (pp. 6, 10). Radar-CEnet: tested over SNR, antennas, pilots, subcarriers; CDL-E trained on 50,000 samples (pp. 12-13).
baselines: Channel estimation: ISTA-GS, SOMP (non-learned), LISTA-GS (learned). DOA: MUSIC, FFT, OMP, ANM (non-learned), plain CNN (learned) (pp. 11-12).
metrics: NMSE in dB for channel estimation versus SNR, antennas, pilots, subcarriers; RMSE of DOA estimation versus SNR and imperfection scaling factor (p. 11).
complexity: Per-layer order O(4Q N_RF G K + 4 G^2 K) for Radar-CEnet and LISTA-GS, O(4Q N_RF G K) per ISTA-GS iteration, O(4L Q N_RF G K) for SOMP; no runtime (p. 12).
q1_support: p. 13: "we generate CDL-E channel data based on the 3GPP TR 38.901 standard using the Sionna simulation platform"; Radar-CEnet is trained on 50,000 and tested on 3,000 of these samples. The main results (Figs. 8-11) use a custom geometric channel (p. 4).
q2_support: p. 6: "Meta-testing refers to the ability of the network to quickly adapt and perform DOA estimation in the case of imperfect arrays", by fine-tuning the meta-trained parameters. This concerns the DOA module; Radar-CEnet itself is not tested outside its training conditions.
q3_support: p. 11: "The proposed Radar-CEnet is compared with the traditional CS algorithms ISTA-GS and SOMP [41], as well as the DL method LISTA-GS." Compared on NMSE in Figs. 8-12 (pp. 12-13).
q4_support: p. 12: "their per-layer computational complexity is the same" for LISTA-GS and Radar-CEnet, O(4Q N_RF G K + 4 G^2 K); ISTA-GS and SOMP orders are also given. No runtime or parameter count.
q5_support: p. 13: "we generate CDL-E channel data based on the 3GPP TR 38.901 standard using the Sionna simulation platform". Self-generated data from a simulator; the paper gives no code or data link and uses no public dataset.
notes: Area 2: the learned Radar-CEnet estimates the communication channel in an ISAC system (p. 1, p. 7), and the main metric is NMSE (p. 11). The MAML-CNN DOA estimator is a sub-module that supplies the angle prior (p. 5-6); DOA alone would be out of scope, but it is not the paper's function. q1 rests on the secondary CDL-E experiment (p. 13), as the main results use a custom geometric model with Gaussian path gains (p. 4). q2 is borderline: the paper describes meta-testing with fine-tuning on new imperfect arrays (p. 6, Fig. 4) but does not say that the arrays of Figs. 6-7 were held out from the 100 meta-training tasks (p. 10); the sweeps over SNR, antennas, pilots and subcarriers (pp. 12-13) do not say whether the network was retrained. q3: LISTA-GS is an earlier learned sparse-recovery network applied here to the same problem (p. 7, p. 11); ISTA-GS and SOMP are non-learned. q5: Sionna is an open simulator, but no generated dataset or code is released.
